column1: Solutions How can the economy get out of a liquidity trap? First, it is worth noting that, in general, optimal monetary policy in the absence of nominal rigidities requires that the nominal interest rate equal zero. Rather than being a bad outcome, converging to a zero nominal interest rate is optimal because it eliminates the wedge between the private and social opportunity costs of money. If, however, for reasons not specified in the simple model used here, the liquidity trap equilibrium is a bad outcome, then one must question the assumption that the policymaker follows an ad hoc nonoptimal decision rule such as (10.13).
